prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a low-speed head-on collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has whiplash. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1228; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my name on a recording, if that's all right. I can answer your questions.

Q: That's fine. For the record, you were the driver of the vehicle involved in the collision in Pasadena, Texas, correct?

A: Yes, I was driving.

Q: Can you describe what happened?

A: I was heading down the road at a slow speed, maybe twenty-five miles an hour. The other car came over into my lane and we hit nose to nose. It wasn't a hard hit, but it was enough to jerk me forward and then back.

Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?

A: Yes, and the airbags did not deploy. I think the belt caught me across the chest.

Q: Did you feel any injuries right after the collision?

A: Not right away. I was a little shaken, but I drove myself to the parking lot and sat for a while. By the evening my neck was stiff and I had a headache that went into my shoulders.

Q: Have you sought medical treatment?

A: Yes, I went to an urgent care center the next day. They diagnosed whiplash and gave me a neck brace and some muscle relaxers. I've also started physical therapy twice a week.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes. Turning my head to check my blind spot is painful, and I can't sleep through the night without waking up because of the pain. Some days I have trouble lifting my grocery bags.

Q: Did you have any neck or back problems before the collision?

A: No, not that I can recall. I'd never had treatment for my neck before.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?

A: Only that I'm following my doctor's instructions and I want to get back to normal as soon as I can.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the statement.
